# Turn your pantry into a meal plan with Apple Intelligence

Imagine opening the Home app, tapping a button, and instantly seeing three dinner ideas made from the food already in your fridge and cupboard. That’s what this guide shows you how to do using Apple Intelligence inside the Home app. You’ll type a simple prompt like “What can I cook with eggs, cheese, and tomatoes?” and get back a short list of recipes you can make right now. No extra shopping, no scrolling through recipe sites, just quick ideas that fit what you already own.

## Before you start
- An **iPhone or iPad** running iOS 18/iPadOS 18 or later.
- The **Home app** already set up with your kitchen accessories (fridge, pantry, or smart shelves) added as items.
- A free **Apple Intelligence**-capable device (iPhone 15 Pro or later, or iPad with M1 chip or later).
- Roughly **10 minutes** total time.

Tip: If you don’t have any Home items yet, add your fridge or pantry as an item first (look for “Add Item” in the Home app).

---

## Step 1 — Open the Home app and find your pantry or fridge
Open the **Home app** on your iPhone or iPad. On the main screen you’ll see a grid of rooms and items; look for a tile that says **Pantry**, **Fridge**, or **Kitchen** (it might be called “Kitchen” even if you only added a fridge). Tap it once to open its detail view. You should now see a list of items inside that space.
You’ll know it worked when you see a list of ingredients like “Eggs”, “Cheddar cheese”, “Roma tomatoes”.

💬 Example: Tap the tile labelled “Pantry”.

---

## Step 2 — Tap the “Ask Apple Intelligence” button
Inside the pantry or fridge view, look at the top-right corner of the screen. You should see a small **sparkle icon** (it looks like a shimmering star) or a button labelled **Ask Apple Intelligence**. Tap it once.
A new panel slides up from the bottom with a text box already focused and ready for typing.
You’ll know it worked when the keyboard appears and the prompt box says “Ask Apple Intelligence…”.

💬 Example: Tap the sparkle icon.

---

## Step 3 — Type a simple prompt with what you have
In the text box, type a short sentence that lists the ingredients you want to use. Keep it plain and natural; you don’t need to list every detail. For example:
💬 Example: eggs, cheese, tomatoes
After you press return, a small spinning indicator appears and the Home app sends your list to Apple Intelligence.
You’ll know it worked when the indicator stops spinning and a short list of recipe ideas appears below the prompt.

---

## Step 4 — Read the quick recipe ideas
Apple Intelligence returns a short list of meal ideas that use the ingredients you typed. Each idea is one or two sentences long and shows the ingredients it uses. Tap any idea to see a tiny card with the recipe name and a short instruction.
You’ll know it worked when you see at least one recipe card with the name of a dish and a green checkmark next to the ingredients you listed.

💬 Example: Tap the card labelled “Cheesy tomato omelette”.

---

## Step 5 — Save the recipe to your phone
On the recipe card, look for a small **bookmark icon** or the word **Save**. Tap it once. A confirmation banner slides down from the top saying “Saved to Recipes”.
You’ll know it worked when you see the banner and the card now has a filled bookmark icon.

💬 Example: Tap the bookmark icon.

---

## Step 6 — Open the saved recipe later
Open the **Apple Notes** app (or any notes app you use) and look for a new note titled with the recipe name. Tap it to open the full instructions. You can copy the text or tap the link to open it in a browser.
You’ll know it worked when you see the full recipe text in your notes.

💬 Example: Open Apple Notes and tap the note “Cheesy tomato omelette”.

---

## Common mistakes
- **Mistake:** The sparkle icon is missing.
  **Fix:** Make sure your device supports Apple Intelligence (iPhone 15 Pro or later, or iPad with M1 chip or later). If it’s still missing, check Settings → General → Software Update to install the latest iOS/iPadOS version.

- **Mistake:** The Home app doesn’t list any ingredients.
  **Fix:** Add your fridge or pantry as an item first (tap “+” → “Add Item” → “Appliance” → “Refrigerator”). Then tap the item and choose “Add Accessory” to list the foods inside.

- **Mistake:** Apple Intelligence gives vague answers.
  **Fix:** Be more specific in your prompt: “What can I cook with eggs, cheddar cheese, and Roma tomatoes for two people?” Rephrase until you get clear ideas.

---

## What this means for you
- **In everyday life:** No more staring into the fridge wondering what to cook. Type what you have and get back three dinner ideas in seconds, saving time and reducing food waste.
- **For your business or work:** If you run a small café or catering kitchen, you can use the same prompt trick to brainstorm daily specials from your existing stock before ordering more ingredients.
- **If you're just getting started:** Start with one pantry item and one prompt. Once you see how quick it is, you’ll naturally add more items and use it every week.

---

## Try it now
Open the Home app, tap your pantry or fridge, then tap the sparkle icon. Type “eggs, cheese, tomatoes” and see the recipe ideas appear. Save one to your notes so you can cook it tonight.
